correctness.rationale: For all N>=3 and q=p^a, projective rank r yields exactly m=N-r rational vanishing transverse directions; the local divisor is the m-variable Moore determinant times a unit. Each determinant term contains a q^(m-1)-power; Frobenius raises it into the p^s-power maximal ideal at the stated exponent. Its nonzero unique lex-leading monomial proves noncontainment at the preceding power for every s, giving the exact threshold. The Gaussian-binomial formula counts kernel choices and injections, divided by projective scalars. Sparse modular multiplication and independent matrix-rank counts verified all listed small examples, including q=4.

originality.rationale: The determinant factorization and the general F-threshold framework are known. The full rank-by-rank exact exponent identity, its pointwise geometric formulation in all N>=3, and finite-extension multiplicity formulas were compared against the broad and most plausible primary results. The 2020 extremal lemma yields an upper bound and covers the binary boundary, not the higher-dimensional equality and distribution. No identified source logically implies the complete claim without additional arguments. Specialist-priority risk remains.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete pointwise classification of first positive test-ideal jumping invariants for a classical reduced free hyperplane divisor in every projective dimension and every finite field size. The exact Frobenius-level certificate and Gaussian-binomial arithmetic point distributions add structural reproducible information beyond a lone threshold value. The drop of thresholds along rational flats is characteristic-dependent and potentially relevant to mod-p singularity benchmarks; no downstream conjecture is assumed.
